1	# CODEBASE_EXPLAINED.md — SuperGrok1.5 exhaustive architectural reference
2	
3	> **Purpose.** A single, self-contained reference: a senior engineer should be able to read this and
4	> fully understand how the system works — and resume development — without re-reading the codebase.
5	> Authored 2026-06-17 by 5 parallel deep-readers (read-only, refute-by-default), every concrete claim
6	> cited as `file:line`. Companion docs: `SESSION_STATE.md` (live resume state), `PLANNING_INPUT.md`
7	> (opportunity map + open decisions), `.perf/phase1_status_audit.md` (the audit this was built on).
8	
9	## Overview — the mental model
10	
11	SuperGrok1.5 trains **3 model families** (transformer decoder, ViT, Mamba-3) under **11 optimizers**
12	= **33 cells**, each compiled as a **single fused persistent CUDA megakernel** on H100 (bf16 wgmma).
13	The defining decision: **one kernel launch runs the entire training step** — forward, backward,
14	gradient reduction, *and* the optimizer update — with phases separated only by an in-kernel,
15	hand-built grid barrier. No per-step relaunch, no cooperative launch, optimizer state stays resident.
16	This is the "one binary, one launch" thesis: it removes launch latency and HBM round-trips between
17	ops, at the cost of pinning **one CTA per SM** (the grid barrier needs all CTAs co-resident).
18	
19	`compile.py` is a **superoptimizer / autotuner**: it JIT-builds, fp64-gates, and times flag / macro /
20	structural variants per cell and bakes per-TU winners, with a learned cost-model and an in-loop
21	correctness gate. Every change — by hand or by the autotuner — must clear the **HARD gate**: fp64
22	parity (rel 1e-4; SAM 2.5e-2) **and** A/A/A bit-determinism (identical across 3 runs). Legal rewrites
23	are **transport-only** (they may move data but must preserve the ascending-k fp32 reduction order, so
24	parity + determinism hold); anything that changes numerics is gate-arbitrated under a keep/revert ratchet.
25	
26	**Performance posture (read §4 closely).** At small/medium scale the system is **latency /
27	serialization-bound** — the decoder runs at ~6.5% of the 989 TF/s bf16 roofline at d=2048. That gap is
28	*largely fixable* (grid-barrier serialization, sub-cuBLAS hand-rolled wgmma, non-GEMM work serialized
29	rather than overlapped, 1-CTA/SM occupancy), **not** a non-GEMM physics floor. The design goal is a
30	high roofline % at **every** scale; the files are meant to optimize for the project they are dropped into.
31	
32	## Contents
33	1. **The model megakernels (decoder / vit / mamba3) + the L3-TC substrate** — the persistent kernel, the GridBarrier, the wgmma + cp.async-ring substrate, the phase structure, per-model specifics.
34	2. **The optimizer files (the 11 optimizers + the fused P3 tail)** — the one-launch fusion, opt_id dispatch, per-optimizer mechanisms (incl. the SuperGrok family), the perf + correctness reality.
35	3. **compile.py — the superoptimizer / autotuner** — the search, the in-loop fp64 gate, macro-injection + drift guard, the Level-2 work, portability, the build env.
36	4. **Why it is latency-bound + the roofline reality + the perf methods** — the measured numbers, the phase breakdown, the mechanisms, the scale-dependence, the keep/revert ratchet.
37	5. **The correctness methodology** — the fp64 + A/A/A HARD gate, transport-only rewrites, the ratchet, the fake-green / oracle-trust hazards and how they are caught.
38	
39	---
40	
41	## The model megakernels (decoder / vit / mamba3) + the L3-TC substrate
42	
43	This section documents the heart of the system: the three per-model persistent megakernels and the hand-built Hopper tensor-core substrate (wgmma + cp.async ring + grid barrier) they all share. Every concrete claim cites `file:line`.
44	
45	### 1. The persistent-megakernel design — one `__global__` per train step
46	
47	The defining structural decision is that an *entire training step* — forward pass, backward pass, gradient reduction, and the optimizer update — runs inside **one** `__global__` kernel launch, with phases separated only by in-kernel grid barriers. There is **no per-step relaunch** and **no cooperative launch**.
48	
49	- **Decoder** entry point: `fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<Opt>` (`csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:672-678`) launched by `launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<Opt>` (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:1511-1569`). The plain triple-chevron launch `fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<Opt><<<grid, block, dyn_smem, stream>>>` (`:1566`) is an ordinary kernel launch — **not** `cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel`.
50	- **ViT**: `fused_vit_megakernel_tc<Opt>` / `launch_fused_vit_megakernel_tc` (`csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_vit_megakernel.cuh:1178`).
51	- **Mamba3**: `fused_mamba_megakernel_tc<Opt>` (`csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_mamba_megakernel.cuh:527-532`), launched at `fused_mamba_megakernel.cuh:349`.
52	
53	The host-side seams that wire these into the Python `_ops` extension are the `*_launcher.cu` TUs: `mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu`, `mega_vit_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu`, `mega_mamba_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu`. Each exposes ONE non-template host launcher with a plain pointers/ints + `FusedScalars` POD boundary so `dispatch.cpp` can `extern`-declare it without any header-only types crossing the ABI (`mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu:14-24`). The launcher TU exists specifically because the Fork-B TC cell driver (`mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc.cu`) owns its own `PYBIND11_MODULE` and is dropped from `_ops` by `setup.py`'s `_collect()` (PyInit collision) — so without this globbed-in seam the bf16 race path had no way to reach the TC kernel and silently ran eager (`:5-11`). The launcher is compiled per-TU with `-DSG_TUNED_GEMM_IMPL=1` (`mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu:30`) to select the wgmma branch.
54	
55	**Grid shape: gridDim.x == #SMs, one persistent CTA per SM.** The launcher reads the SM count via `cudaDeviceGetAttribute(..., cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount, ...)` and launches exactly that many CTAs: `launch_ctas = (unsigned)n_sms; ctx.n_ctas = launch_ctas` (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:1547-1549`). The optional `ncta_cap` argument (default 0 = full saturation; the race always passes 0) lets a memory-constrained test launch fewer CTAs (`:1504-1510`).
56	
57	**Why one CTA/SM.** The grid barrier (below) rendezvouses all `n_ctas` CTAs at every phase boundary; this can only complete if every launched CTA is *simultaneously resident*. So the launcher hard-gates occupancy ≥ 1 with the *actual* dynamic smem and **refuses to launch otherwise** rather than risk a hang: `cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor(...); if (occ < 1) return cudaErrorLaunchOutOfResources` (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:1540-1545`). The scalar fallback launcher makes the rationale explicit in its assert: "0 blocks/SM — GridBarrier would hang" (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:317-321`). Pinning one CTA per SM (via `sm_id()` reading `%smid`, `megakernel_common.cuh:65-73`) also keeps that SM's optimizer-state slice warm in its L2 partition across the whole step (`megakernel_common.cuh:57-63`).
58	
59	**Why fusion instead of relaunch.** A conventional pipeline relaunches a kernel per op (fwd GEMM, bwd GEMM, dW GEMM, optimizer step), paying launch latency and round-tripping every activation/gradient through HBM between launches. The megakernel keeps activations and the reduced gradient resident in an HBM workspace it owns and never tears down the grid, so the only cross-phase synchronization cost is the in-kernel barrier — no launch overhead, no driver round-trips, and the optimizer state stays L2-resident on its owning SM.
60	
61	**Why not cooperative launch.** Cooperative grid sync (`cooperative_groups::grid_group::sync()`) requires `cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel`, which caps the launchable grid at the number of CTAs that can be co-resident *and is itself subject to the cooperative-launch CTA ceiling*. The hand-built `GridBarrier` (below) needs no cooperative launch, so it "scales past the cooperative-grid CTA cap" (`megakernel_common.cuh:27-29`).
62	
63	### 2. The hand-built GridBarrier (`megakernel_common.cuh`)
64	
65	`GridBarrier` (`megakernel_common.cuh:147-255`) is a reusable arrive/wait grid barrier built from **two global atomics plus a sense-reversing generation counter**:
66	
67	- `g_arrived` — count of CTAs that have reached the current barrier.
68	- `g_generation` — the sense-reversing generation, advanced once each time the barrier is crossed (`:148-150`).
69	
70	All state is host-zero-initialized; the launcher re-zeros all three counters per launch with `cudaMemsetAsync` (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:1557-1559`). `PersistentContext` bundles these device pointers + `n_tasks` + `n_ctas` into the uniform kernel signature (`megakernel_common.cuh:263-276`).
71	
72	**The mechanism** (`GridBarrier::sync()`, `:157-210`):
73	1. `__syncthreads()` so the whole CTA reaches the barrier before its leader publishes.
74	2. Thread 0 samples `my_gen = *(volatile)g_generation` (the sense it is waiting to leave).
75	3. **§1.14 RELEASE**: `__threadfence()` makes this CTA's phase writes visible device-wide *before* arrival is announced (`:166-169`).
76	4. `prev = atomicAdd(g_arrived, 1)`. The CTA whose add completes the set (`prev+1 == n_ctas`) is the **last arriver**: it `atomicExch(g_arrived, 0)` to clear the count for the next phase, `__threadfence()`, then `atomicAdd(g_generation, 1)` — order matters so an observer of the new generation also sees `arrived==0` (`:173-182`).
77	5. **Everyone else spins** on `(volatile)g_generation == my_gen` (`:194-200`).
78	6. **§1.14 ACQUIRE**: after observing the generation advance, `__threadfence()` so peers' released phase writes are visible (`:203-205`), then a closing `__syncthreads()` releases the rest of the block (`:208-209`).
79	
80	**Why sense-reversing beats a naive counter reset.** The classic hazard with a counter barrier is *reuse*: if you just reset `arrived=0`, a fast CTA can enter the *next* barrier and increment the counter before a slow CTA has even observed the release of the *previous* one (`:128-134`). The generation counter fixes this — a late CTA waits for the generation to *advance* (the consumer side never touches `arrived` for reset), so an early CTA cannot lap it.
81	
82	**Why `__nanosleep` backoff.** A tight `volatile`-read spin hammers the L2/memory subsystem and steals issue slots from the still-arriving (laggard) CTAs. The waiter instead parks with `__nanosleep(backoff)` on an exponentially growing nap capped at 1024 ns: `backoff = (backoff < 1024u) ? (backoff << 1) : 1024u` (`:193-199`). This is behavior-preserving — it exits the instant the generation advances; only the *poll cadence* changes (sm_70+; a no-op fallback on older arches).
83	
84	**The fused reset (`sync_reset`, `:222-254`).** The L3 phase loop needs the task-queue counter zeroed between the reduce phase and the optimizer phase. Rather than `sync → reset → sync` (which would cost 4 grid barriers + 2 standalone resets per step), the reset is folded into the last-arriver critical section: the last CTA does `atomicExch(g_arrived,0)` **and** `atomicExch(reset_counter,0)` *before* the release-store that bumps the generation, so any CTA that later observes the new generation is guaranteed to see `reset_counter==0`. This collapses 4 grid barriers → 2 per step with identical ordering/visibility (`:213-221`). It is invoked as `bar.sync_reset(ctx.g_next_task)` (e.g. `fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:953`).
85	
86	**Minimal fences (§1.14).** The doctrine is exactly one `__threadfence()` before the arrival publish and one after the wait — the minimum for a correct release/acquire pair (`:34, 136-142`). A loose extra fence here is "both a correctness and a >10% perf footgun" (`:32-34`).
87	
88	**TaskQueue / work-stealing.** Alongside the barrier, `TaskQueue` (`:91-117`) is a single global atomic counter (`g_next_task`). `next_block(smem_slot)` has the leader thread do one `atomicAdd` and broadcast the claimed parameter-tensor index to the whole CTA via shared memory (`:108-116`). There is no static partition — an idle CTA simply calls `next_block()` again, so a CTA that drains its tensor early steals the next one; the atomic *is* the steal (`:75-90`). Determinism is preserved because the work-steal queue only picks *who* reduces an element range, never the *order* of the fp32 summation within it (see P2 below).

90	### 3. The in-kernel phase structure (decoder TC, the reference layout)
91	
92	The decoder TC kernel body (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:672-1502`) is the canonical 5-phase / 4-barrier layout (`:18-37`); the ViT and Mamba kernels mirror it. Phase-by-phase, with the staged-optimizer insertions:
93	
94	- **P0 (zero + weight pre-stage)** — each CTA zeroes its own LN-vec partials and loss slot (`:810-811`), and converts the fp32 params to the bf16 weight cache `wbf_cache` (C1) grid-strided and element-owned (`dectc_wbf_convert`, `:814`). No host memset; each CTA owns its slice → no cross-CTA contention.
95	- **B0** (`bar.sync()`, `:818`) — fences the bf16 weight cache and zeroed partials before any P1 GEMM reads them.
96	- **(P1 window) embedding list build** — CTA 0 builds the counting-sort token lists *here*, overlapping the other CTAs' fwd/bwd (`dectc_embed_build_lists`, `:828-829`), so the already-present B1 barrier fences it for P2 with **no new barrier**.
97	- **P1 (token-tile fwd+bwd GEMMs)** — each CTA grid-strides over tiles of `kTileM` rows (`:840`); per tile it runs `dectc_forward_tile` → NLL, then `dectc_backward_tile` → writes activations X, output adjoints dY, embedding-input adjoint dh0, and LN-vec partials (`:847-868`). Barrier-free within a tile. Loss accumulated fp32 per CTA into `loss_part[cta]` (`:866, 869`).
98	- **B1** (`:877`) — all activations (X + dY) + LN-vec partials complete.
99	- **P2 (dW GEMM + grad assembly)** — builds the 9 dW specs into shared smem (thread 0; identical for all threads, keeping the spec array off every thread's stack, `:890-897`); runs the dW GEMMs (split-K or single-CTA, §6 below, `:919-931`); then assembles biases (`dectc_dw_biases`), the embedding owner-scan (`dectc_embed_owner_scan`), and the deterministic LN-vec reduce (`dectc_lnvec_reduce`) (`:937-939`). The loss is reduced in **fp64** by CTA 0 only — `double s = Σ loss_part[c]; mean = s/B` — because the 1e-5 loss rel-tol is the tightest gate and fp32-summing ~4191 terms can miss it (`:940-945, 33`).
100	- **B2** = `bar.sync_reset(ctx.g_next_task)` (`:953`) — reduced grad ready; task queue reset for the optimizer phase.
101	- **Optional P2.x staged-optimizer phases**, each `if constexpr`-gated so every other cell is byte-identical:
102	  - **P2.4 SAM 2nd backward** (LookSAM / SuperGrok11/15 / SuperGrok2, `:993-1110`): global ‖g‖ deterministic ascending-CTA reduce → `rho_over_norm`; back up params + perturb `p' = p + (ρ/‖g‖)·g`; re-convert the bf16 cache from `p'`; run a **full second in-kernel fwd+bwd + grad assembly** into a separate `sam_grad` buffer; write the side channel (`sam_dir = g_sam−g` for LookSAM, else `sharpness = (g_sam−g)²`) and restore params from backup. Gated to every-k SAM steps by `st.looksam_sam` (`:995`); on intervening steps the cached side channel is reused.
103	  - **P2.5 grad-norm clip** (GrokAdamW / NeuralGrok, `:1128-1167`): global L2 norm via per-CTA partial → CTA0 ascending sum → `clip_coef`, broadcast; grad is not mutated (the coefficient is applied per-element inside the apply).
104	  - **P2.6 Prodigy d-reduce** (`:1205-1251`): a **fixed-partition** (not work-steal) ascending reduce of the cross-all-tensors (r,s) estimator → EMA decay → `d = max(d_prev, d_coef·r_ema/|s_ema|)`. The fixed partition is deliberate: the older work-steal drain regrouped fp32 sums by timing, an A/A/A determinism violation by construction (`:1182-1203`).
105	  - **P2.7 Muon Newton-Schulz** (`:1268-1322`): grid-cooperative NS orthogonalization of the 11 2D weights, one matrix at a time across all CTAs, barrier-looped per NS iteration (`buf=μ·buf+g → ‖buf‖_F → X=buf·inv_norm → {A=XXᵀ, AX, AAX, orth=aX+bAX+cAAX, swap}×5 → apply`).
106	  - **P2.45 / P3-SG2** (SuperGrok11/15/2 meta-net mu precompute and the full SG2 CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU meta-net, `:1338-1409`).
107	- **P3 (optimizer tail)** — work-steal the parameter tensors from the (reset) queue; for each, `apply_optimizer<Opt>` over the reduced grad in-place (`:1411-1498`). No barrier after P3 — the kernel exits and the step is complete.

109	The scalar fp32 fallback kernel (`fused_decoder_megakernel<Opt>`, gated by `SG_DEC_SCALAR_MEGAKERNEL`, `:195-292`) shows the same P0→B0→P1→B1→P2→B2→P3 skeleton in its simplest batch-parallel form (each CTA owns a contiguous batch slice, accumulating into a per-CTA `[nCTA × total]` partial, then a deterministic ascending-CTA reduce). It is gated off at large `d` because its per-sample `DecSampleSmem` grows with `SG_DEC_D` and ptxas hard-stops (`:129-138`); the TC engine's `DecTcSmem` is `d`-independent.

111	The Mamba TC kernel uses the **same** P0/B0/P1/B1/P2/B2/P3 structure but in the batch-parallel scalar-engine form (each CTA owns a contiguous batch slice and writes a full `[total]` grad partial; the wgmma-projection dW machinery is bypassed — see §7) (`fused_mamba_megakernel.cuh:22-36, 533-539`).

113	### 4. The wgmma substrate (`csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/wgmma.cuh`)
114	
115	This is the hand-rolled in-kernel `ss`-wgmma (shared-shared: both operands in smem) for `wgmma.mma_async.sync.aligned.m64nNk16.f32.bf16.bf16`. It deliberately does **not** use CUTLASS — host-launched CUTLASS collectives are not device-callable and are rejected for the persistent-megakernel path (`wgmma.cuh:14-18`). Every asm sequence cites its PTX ISA section (`:28-29`).
116	
117	**Descriptor bit-packing (`make_smem_desc`, `:219-241`).** The 64-bit shared-memory matrix descriptor (PTX §<ip>.4) packs: start address in bits 13:0 (the smem byte address `>>4`, so the low 4 bits must be zero → 16-byte alignment is mandatory or they are silently dropped, `:174-189`), LBO in bits 29:16 (`>>4`), SBO in bits 45:32 (`>>4`), base-offset in 51:49, and the swizzle/layout mode in 63:62 (`:231-235`). The canonical Major-K builders `make_desc_A_kmajor<MN>` / `make_desc_B_kmajor<N>` compute `LBO = MN*16` bytes (one core-matrix block) and `SBO = 128` bytes (8 MN-rows × 16 B/row) for the no-swizzle INTERLEAVE layout, verified against `cute::make_gmma_desc<Major::K>` (`:261-288`).
118	
119	**LayoutType / swizzle encoding (`SwizzleMode`, `:167-172`).** A documented footgun: the layout-type field bits 63:62 are **not** size-ascending — the correct CUTLASS encoding is `NONE=0, SWIZZLE_128B=1, SWIZZLE_64B=2, SWIZZLE_32B=3` (an earlier draft had 32B/128B swapped, `:151-155`). The correctness path ships `kSwizzleNone` (a fully legal mode and the layout the gates validate against torch); 128B-swizzle is a dormant perf-phase template arg (`:156-165`).
120	
121	**Required smem operand layout (`:250-259`).** For an `MN×16` bf16 operand, element `(mn,k)` lives at bf16 index `idx(mn,k) = (k/8)*(MN*8) + mn*8 + (k%8)` — i.e. K=16 is two stacked 8-wide core matrices, each an `MN×8` row-major block of 128-bit rows. The staging loops everywhere (model headers, self-test, tile_pipeline) must write this exact layout.
122	
123	**Fragment decode (`WgmmaAccum<N>` + `wgmma_frag_decode`, `:314-364`).** The per-thread fp32 accumulator holds `N/2` registers (PTX §<ip>.3). The authoritative decode maps `(tid_in_wg, reg i)` → `(row, col)`: the M=64 rows are partitioned warp-major (`row = 16*warp + lane/4 + 8*row_half`), and the N columns are held as n8 column slabs (`col = (lane&3)*2 + col_par + 8*slab`) (`:357-362`). Keeping ONE decode shared by the epilogue store and the gate's reference comparison eliminates the chance of a mismatched private decode (`:310-312`).
124	
125	**Fence/commit/wait choreography (`:366-403`).** `wgmma_fence()` (§<ip>.2) makes prior non-wgmma writes to the accumulator/operand-smem visible before the first issue; `wgmma_commit_group()` (§<ip>.5) batches issued MMAs into a group; `wgmma_wait_group<N>()` (§<ip>.6) blocks until ≤N groups remain — the epilogue must `wait_group<0>` before reading the accumulators.
126	
127	**The ascending-k mainloop (`wgmma_mainloop_kchain`, `:617-644`).** Runs `k_steps` ss-wgmma issues in **fixed ascending k-order** (the DESIGN §3.1 determinism rule: one CTA owns the tile end-to-end, no work-steal split, no float atomics → bit-reproducible). The first issue uses `ScaleD=0` (overwrite, so a fresh accumulator needs no zeroing), the rest `ScaleD=1` (accumulate); one `wgmma_fence()` before the group, one `commit_group()+wait_group<0>()` after. The descriptor generator is a callback `gen(k)`, which is what lets the *same* mainloop serve both the unpipelined gate (fixed pre-staged array) and the pipelined gate (ring-buffer stage) with bit-identical numerics (`:603-609`). The per-N issue overloads (`wgmma_issue_n8/16/32/64/96/128`, `:441-561`) each name exactly `N/2` `+f` accumulator registers; N=128 (default tile, 64 regs) is the in/out/ff GEMM shape.

129	### 5. The cp.async multi-stage ring (`tile_pipeline.cuh` + the PIPE/STAGES macros)
130	
131	`tile_pipeline.cuh` adds the producer/consumer ring choreography on top of the wgmma engine, reusing `Mbarrier`/`cp_async_cg_16`/`cp_async_wait_group` rather than redefining them (`tile_pipeline.cuh:9-17`). It uses **cp.async (`.cg.16`), not TMA** — TMA is explicitly phase-2 (`:199-200`). A `TilePipeline<N,Depth>` (`:142-189`) manages a Depth-stage ring of `(A 64×16 + B N×16)` bf16 tiles plus `2*Depth` mbarriers — a `full[s]` (producer arrives via `arrive_expect_tx` when a stage's loads are issued; consumer waits before wgmma) and an `empty[s]` (consumer arrives when done; producer waits before overwriting, WAR-safe) per stage (`:117-135`). Each barrier expects a **full warpgroup (128) of arrivals** — a per-warp `elect_one` would give 4 arrivals on a count-1 barrier and deadlock the parity wait, a bug called out explicitly (`:170-179`). `tc_pipelined_gemm_m64nNk16` (`:271-364`) splits the 256-thread CTA into WG0 (producer: cp.async-stages each K-tile, `:296-312`) and WG1 (consumer: wgmma in ascending k, `:313-360`), with the `setmaxnreg` register rebalance (producer few regs, consumer many) via `SG_TUNED_PROD_REGS=40 / SG_TUNED_CONS_REGS=232` (`:92-97, 289-294`). Determinism: the consumer issues the SAME ss-wgmma sequence in the SAME ascending-k order, so the pipeline only changes *when* an operand becomes available, not the math (`:265-269`).

134	- `SG_TUNED_DEC_GEMM_STAGES` (the base K-loop double-buffer depth; default 2, `:90-92`).

This is an allocation change only — identical layout / access pattern / fp32 accumulation order / wgmma issue sequence → parity by construction (`:439-442`). The dW path always keeps the synchronous (lambda-source) staging — it is staging-bound, not drain-bound, so a ring would be the wrong lever (`:782-783`).

144	### 6. Decoder specifics
145	
146	- **Causal attention** — `dectc_forward_tile` runs per-sample causal self-attention (`model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:1433`); the head is masked `kj > qi`, in contrast to ViT's bidirectional attention. The final-norm + head + CE run on the **last** position (`kSeq-1`).
147	- **Embedding counting-sort owner-scan** — the embedding gradient is a scatter-add of `dh0` into a small set of vocab rows. The H2 design (`:2418-2446`) uses a deterministic integer counting sort: `dectc_embed_build_lists` (`:2469-2527`) builds CSR offsets `row_start[V+1]` + a permutation `perm[T]` (token positions bucketed by vocab row, ascending-t within each row) once on CTA 0 in the P1 window. The consume `dectc_embed_owner_scan` is a flat grid-stride over all `V·d` output elements where element `(r,j)` walks only row r's tokens in ascending-t order, reading `dh0[perm[i]·d+j]`. This collapses work to `O(d·T)` with coalesced reads and keeps all 132 CTAs busy. **Determinism**: per-row accumulation is the same fixed ascending-t order as the old scan → bit-identical fp32, no atomics (`:2435-2439`). The build's per-(worker,row) cursor uses an ascending-worker prefix within a row so lower-t chunks land first — globally ascending t per bucket (`:2501-2513`).
148	- **dW split-K (`SG_TUNED_DEC_DW_SPLITK`)** — chunks the dW `K=T` contraction across CTAs so the ~62% idle SMs in P2 do real work (`:86-88`). `dectc_dw_run_tile_splitk<N>` (`:2295-2339`) computes a PARTIAL over K-chunk `kc` of `G` into a per-(tile,chunk) scratch slot with a **floor-balanced partition** `k0=floor(kc·KS/G), k1=floor((kc+1)·KS/G)` — near-equal, summing to KS exactly for any KS≥G (a ceil split would leave a trailing empty chunk whose unwritten slot sums garbage; the floor never empties one, `:2288-2294`), with an explicit empty-chunk guard zeroing the slot (`:2318-2322`). `dectc_dw_reduce_splitk` (`:2343-2366`) then sums the G chunk-partials in **ascending kc** → deterministic. The default is now **G=1** (`:101`): with DW_STAGE=1 the single-CTA dW is 2.05× faster than G=2-scalar, making split-K (a scalar-dW grid-fill mitigation) obsolete (`:98-100`).
149	- **The DW_STAGE staging method (`SG_TUNED_DEC_DW_STAGE`, default 1)** — the dW GEMM is **staging-bound, not drain-bound**: ~97% of each K-step was the scalar transposed-strided operand gather, only ~3% the wgmma (`:117-124`). So the lever is faster *staging*, not pipelining the MMA. `SG_TUNED_DEC_DW_STAGE=1` does a cheap grid-cooperative pre-transpose (`dectc_dw_transpose_operands`, `:2088`) writing each weight's dY/X once per step into a **contiguous K-major** scratch (`dYt[Nout,K], Xt[Kin,K]`, K-contiguous + 16B-aligned), so the dW then builds `DecGmemTileSrcA/B` over it and reuses the existing cp.async ring's 16-byte coalesced copies instead of the 2-byte strided gather (`:132-143`). It changes transport only — fp64 parity + A/A/A by construction. `kDecDwTransposeActive = (DW_STAGE==1) && (DW_SPLITK==1)` (`:1994`); when active, an extra B1b barrier fences the transposed operands before any dW GEMM read (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:910-915`).

151	### 7. ViT specifics
152	
153	ViT is a genuine rewrite (separate header `model_stage_vit_tc.cuh`) with four deltas vs the decoder twin (`:21-32`): (1) **full bidirectional attention** — no causal mask, every key contributes for every query (`:22-24, 764`); (2) patch-proj `Linear(49→128)` replaces token embedding, with a learned CLS token prepended at position 0 and a `pos[17]` table; (3) the CLS pos-0 head (final-norm + head + CE run on position 0, not the last); (4) `kSeq=17` forces `kTileM = LCM(17,64) = 1088` (17 stacked m64 atoms = 64 samples × 17 positions).
154	
155	**The B1 sub-tile lever (`SG_TUNED_VIT_P1_SUBTILE_S`, baked at 8).** Because the GEMM tile is locked at 1088 rows, at B=1024 there are only `n_tiles=16` P1 tiles, so **116 of 132 CTAs do zero P1 work and spin at B1** the whole fwd+bwd — tile-count-vs-SM quantization, the #1 ViT cost (51.2% of the step) (`:125-131`). This knob decouples the P1 *scheduling* granularity from the 1088 GEMM lock: P1 grid-strides over sub-tiles of **S whole samples** (`kSeq·S` rows) instead of whole 1088-row tiles, growing `n_tiles` ~`64/S`× so the idle CTAs pick up work and the B1 spin collapses (`:133-137`). S must stay a *whole-sample* count — never split a 17-row sample across CTAs, which would corrupt attention (`:137-141`). The sub-tile row count `kSeq·S` is generally not a multiple of 64, so the small GEMMs pad M up to `ceil(rows/64)·64` atoms with a runtime `m_real` row-guard making the pad rows inert and race-free (`:139-141, 373-391`). **Default 64** (== `kSamplesPerTile`) makes the build byte-identical (the `m_real` guard + runtime-m_atoms code is `#if`'d out at S==64, `:143-147`). The P1 loop using `kVitP1SubtileRows` is at `fused_vit_megakernel.cuh:588-613`. **Parity**: dW/biases/cls/pos grads are byte-identical (P2 reads acts by global token row, contracts ascending-k independent of P1 tiling); the LN-affine γ/β grads + loss are valid fp32 reassociations absorbed by the 1e-4 reorder tol; A/A/A holds because S is a fixed deterministic partition (`:150-162`). The baked verdict: **S=8 is parity-clean (11/11 ViT cells × 3 seeds) and fastest — 4.02× vs S=64 OFF at d=2048/B=1024** (`:164-169`).
156	
157	ViT P2 is dW-output-stationary (`vittc_dw_run_tile` or split-K, `:642-648`) plus biases, the cls/pos owner-scan (`vittc_clspos_owner_scan`, `:656`), and the LN-vec reduce (`:657`).
158	
159	### 8. Mamba3 specifics
160	
161	Mamba3 (`model_stage_mamba3.cuh`) is the genuine Mamba-3 SISO architecture (arXiv 2603.15569, ICLR 2026) transcribed line-for-line from the fp64-verified oracle (`:8-15`). The mixer is a complex **exponential-trapezoidal selective scan** (Eq 25, the heart of the kernel):
162	
163	`v_t = Bbar_t ⊙ x_t; h_t = alpha_t·(R_t@h_{t-1}) + beta_t·(R_t@v_{t-1}) + gamma_t·v_t; y_t = Σ_{c,d} Cbar_t[c,d]·h_t` with `alpha=exp(dt·A), gamma=lam·dt, beta=(1-lam)·dt·alpha` per head and a 2×2 rotation `R(phi)` per complex coord (`:41-46`).
164	
165	**Per-coord state / the seq=8 register exploit.** Parallelization is batch-parallel (Option B, identical to the decoder scalar design): each CTA owns a fixed contiguous batch slice and the whole CTA cooperates on one sample at a time (`:52-62`). The scan exploit: **one thread owns SSM channel `j ∈ [0,d_inner)`**, and within its head holds the complex state `h[Nc][2]` in **registers**, unrolling `t=0..kSeq-1` (`mb_scan_fwd`, `:521-568`). Because seq=8 is tiny, the backward recomputes the forward keeping the full `h_hist`/`v_hist` in registers — **no checkpointing** (`:56-58, 570-574`). A subtle constraint: the per-coord arrays (`hr/hi/vpr/vpi`, `kStateC=64` each) are runtime-indexed local memory, and the c-loop is intentionally *not* `#pragma unroll`'d — a full unroll would force >255 registers and the carried state wouldn't persist across the t-loop (the documented "t=0 right, t>0 wrong" bug, `:527-531`).
166	
167	**Why MambaSampleSmem caps placement at ~d=142.** The per-CTA `MambaSampleSmem` (`:142-202`) caches **both layers'** forward activations (`x_in`, `z`, `Bbar`, `Cbar`, `y_scan`, SwiGLU internals, etc.), and these widths scale with `d`/`d_inner`. The struct exceeds the 48 KB static cap, so it must live in **dynamic smem** opted-in via `cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize(kMambaSmemBytes)` (`:64-68`; `mamba3_layout.cuh:257-264`). At the production `d=128` it is `kMambaSmemFloats=53961` → `kMambaSmemBytes=215844` (~215 KB), pinned by a `static_assert(sizeof(MambaSampleSmem) == kMambaSmemBytes)` (`:206-208`) and bounded by `static_assert(kMambaSmemBytes <= 228*1024)` (`mamba3_layout.cuh:275-278`). Since the live set scales with `d` and is already at ~215 KB of the ~228 KB/SM opt-in budget at `d=128`, the maximum placeable `d` is only marginally above it — roughly `d≈142` before one CTA/SM can no longer place (which would hang the GridBarrier). 173	## The optimizer files (the 11 optimizers + the fused P3 tail)
174	
175	### The central perf thesis: the optimizer is the megakernel's tail, not a separate kernel
176	
177	The single most important design fact in this directory is that **the optimizer update is not a kernel at all** — it is the final phase (P3) of the *same* persistent megakernel that ran forward and backward. One binary, one `<<<>>>` launch per training step, optimizer state HBM-resident, zero kernel round-trips. The phase structure of the decoder megakernel makes this literal: P0 zeroes per-CTA grad partials, P1 does batch-parallel fwd+bwd, P2 deterministically reduces the cross-CTA grad, and **P3 runs the optimizer over the reduced grad in the same grid** (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:216-291`, with the P3 block at `275-291`). There is no grid teardown between the gradient and the weight update — the same CTAs that summed the gradient in P2 work-steal the parameter tensors and apply the update, separated only by one grid barrier (`bar.sync_reset(ctx.g_next_task)` at `:273`, comment "B2: reduced grad ready; reset queue for P3").
178	
179	The P3 tail is a templated work-steal loop over the model's parameter tensors. Each CTA pulls a tensor id `t` from the persistent `TaskQueue`, reads its numel/offset from the `__constant__` `kDecSizes`/`kDecOffsets` tables (so no layout tensors cross the host ABI), rebases the optimizer state pointers to that tensor's slice, and calls `apply_optimizer<Opt>` per element (`:280-290`). The fwd+bwd+reduce is *optimizer-independent* — only this tail differs across the 11 optimizers — which is exactly why the launcher can take a single runtime `opt_id` and pick the kernel instantiation (`mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu:80-98`).
180	
181	**How state is bound (no separate state kernel, no round-trip).** The optimizer's persistent state lives in one flat caller-owned buffer laid out `[m | v | extra]` over `3*total` floats plus a trailing loss slot. The launcher slices it once and binds the slices into a `FusedOptState` POD that is passed by value into the kernel (`mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu:135-185`): `st.exp_avg = state` (m), `st.exp_avg_sq = state + total` (v), `st.ema = state + 2*total` (the `extra` slice). The "extra" slice is overloaded per optimizer — it is the grokfast/grokadamw slow-grad EMA, OR Prodigy's `s` trajectory accumulator, OR LookSAM's cached `sam_dir`, OR SG11/15's per-element `mu` — all aliasing the same region because no optimizer uses more than one of them (`:144-175`). Staged optimizers that need more than `3*total` (Prodigy, SG11/15, SG2) extend the buffer past the loss slot; the host sizes it per-cell in `dispatch.cpp` (`min_state` at `:780-782`: `4*total+4` for Prodigy, `4*total+1+kSgPhiPack` for SG11/15, else `3*total+1`).
182	
183	Inside the kernel, `rebase_state<Opt>` (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:142-163`) takes the base `FusedOptState` and adds the tensor's flat offset to every *per-element* pointer (`exp_avg`, `exp_avg_sq`, `ema`, `sam_dir`, `s_track`, `mu`, `orth`, `smart_grad`, `param_init`, `sharpness`), leaving scalars and *per-tensor* weight sets (the NeuralGrok psi pointers, the SG11/15 phi pointers) un-rebased because those are the same for every element of the tensor (`:159-161`). This is the seam that makes "one resident state buffer, work-stolen by tensor" work.

This is a hand-maintained cross-language contract (Python verdict sets ↔ C++ `OptId` ↔ `dispatch.cpp` int map); the test-coverage audit flags the lack of an automated drift-guard on it as a standing gap (`.perf/test_coverage_gap_audit.json`, rule (e)).

191	The integer is then turned into a kernel template instantiation by a **`switch (static_cast<OptId>(opt_id))`** in each model's launcher TU. 193	### apply_optimizer<Opt>: the real per-element math, single-sourced
194	
195	`apply_optimizer<Opt>` (`opt_components.cuh:380-520`) is a compile-time `if constexpr` ladder; **every branch calls the canonical device function in `csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h`** — there is no re-implementation in the megakernel (the `#include`s are at `opt_components.cuh:33-42`). The scalars an optimizer reads come from `FusedScalars` (`:271-336`), a POD the host fills and `apply_scalars` (`:342-376`) folds into `FusedOptState`. The C2-gap comment (`:248-262`) is load-bearing history: before this struct existed, every cell left `bc1/bc2/gate/d_factor` at their `1.0` struct defaults, silently freezing the math at t=1; `FusedScalars` is the ABI seam that un-freezes them, with defaults chosen to reproduce the old inert behavior exactly so unset fields are byte-identical.
196	
197	**adamw (OptId 0).** `algo::adamw_step` with `bc1`/`bc2` (`:385-388`). The bias corrections are host-computed: `bc1 = 1 - beta1**step`, `bc2 = 1 - beta2**step` (`dispatch.py:_opt_scalars_from` `:1047-1048`), passed un-inverted (the apply divides). One `(bc1,bc2)` pair per call is correct only because the grokking race steps every tensor together — the megakernel treats the whole flat param as one task (`opt_components.cuh:263-269`).

201	**grokfast (OptId 2).** `algo::grokfast_fused_step`, but with a cold-start reseed: `if (step == 1) st.ema[idx] = grad[idx]` (`:392-407`). 202	
203	**grokadamw (OptId 3).** The only tail that legitimately re-inlines (not just calls) (`:408-466`). Three eager mechanisms land: (i) per-tensor layer-wise β1 = β1·(1-γ)^t, with bc1 *also* rebased to 1-β1ᵢ^step — done at the P3 call site (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:1437-1441`) because the work-steal task id `t` *is* the eager `named_parameters()` layer index; (ii) global grad-norm clip, whose coefficient `clip_coef` is computed *on-device* in P2.5 (the deterministic ascending-CTA grad-norm reduction) and applied here; (iii) adaptive α, an in-context no-op because no loss signal is fed. The drift audit flags this EMA/amplification re-inline as the strongest case for extending the guard (it is the same re-inline *class* as the SG11 bug, currently correct but unguarded).
204	
205	**prodigy (OptId 5), the d-reduce phase.** The apply tail is `algo::prodigy_apply_step` reading `st.d_factor` (`:472-476`), but `d_factor` is produced by an **in-kernel staged phase P2.6** between B2 and P3 (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:1205-1251`). This is a global d-adaptation reduction over *every element of every tensor*: each CTA owns a fixed contiguous flat element range `[pe0, pe0+pecnt)` (deliberately NOT the work-steal queue, for determinism by construction — `:1182-1203`), calls the canonical `algo::prodigy_partials_step` accumulating `r = Σ d²·<g, p0−p>` and `s = Σ d²·|g|`, publishes per-CTA `(r,s)` slots, then CTA0 owner-sums ascending, decays the persisted EMAs by `beta3=√β2`, runs `prodigy_update_d` (d = max(d_prev, d_coef·r_ema/|s_ema|)), persists `[r_ema|s_ema|d_lr]`, and broadcasts (`:1234-1250`). The trajectory anchor `p0` is `st.param_init`, bound at `loss_out+1` (`mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc_launcher.cu:159-161`).

207	**muon (OptId 7): Newton-Schulz, the 2D-weight table, the NS phase.** Muon auto-splits parameters by `ndim`: 2D matrices get Newton-Schulz orthogonalization, everything else gets AdamW with *independent* `adamw_lr/adamw_betas` (the `aux_*` fields). 243	The systemic shape behind every caveat (per `test_coverage_gap_audit.json`) is the SG11 bug's shape recurring: the gate suite is blind along four axes at once — single-step-from-zero-init (every momentum/EMA/clip/d/SAM mechanism exercised only where buggy and correct coincide), tiny-scale-only (p=97, d=128, single-CTA-degenerate reductions), a hand-transcribed-mirror-or-co-derived-oracle correctness anchor, and ungated/uncompiled ON-paths for new knobs and the warm/firing/SAM-off branches. These are coverage gaps in the *gate*, not confirmed errors in the *math*.

247	## compile.py — the superoptimizer / autotuner (and the Level-2 work)
248	
249	### What it is
250	
251	`grokking_optimizers/compile.py` (32,900 lines) is a **per-`(optimizer, model, arch)` autotuner and superoptimizer**: it JIT-builds, fp64-correctness-gates, and times a large space of flag / macro / structural kernel variants, then bakes the per-translation-unit winner into the shipped extension. It is the development-time companion to `setup.py` — where `pip install -e .` builds the whole `_ops` extension with default flags, `compile.py` compiles a *focused, maximally-optimized* build for one cell (`compile.py:6-12`). It is invoked as `python -m grokking_optimizers.compile --optimizer <opt> --model <model> --arch <arch>` (`compile.py:96-112`).
252	
253	**Two-phase AOT/JIT pipeline** (`compile.py:14-70`). The work is split so a CPU-only host can do the heavy AOT compile and ship a cache, and the GPU host does the timing sweep:
254	
255	- **AOT phase** (`build_aot`, `compile.py:17409`): resolve sources, hash `(source_set, host_cflags, device_cflags, search_space, pgo_state)`, look up the cell in the on-disk cache (JSON, `CACHE_VERSION == 4`, `compile.py:72-89,195`); on a miss, build with `torch.utils.cpp_extension.load` (ninja, `MAX_JOBS=$(nproc)`, arch-tuned codegen + LTO), record artifact path/size/mtime/SHA-256, mark `aot_completed_at`. No GPU needed.
256	- **JIT phase** (`build_jit`, `compile.py:17693`): load the search space, prefilter, run the autotune driver, pick the winner, write `csrc/algorithms/tuned_configs.h`, persist the winner to the canonical `_kernel_tuned.json`, and rebuild the artifact with the winning macros baked in.
257	- `--runtime {aot,jit,both}` (default `both`) spawns an AOT subprocess (CPU env) then a JIT subprocess (GPU env), each re-entering `main` on the same on-disk cache, so AOT and JIT can be tuned with independent env/library settings (`compile.py:62-70`).
258	
259	**PGO** is optional and AOT-side: with `--pgo`, `build_aot` runs the 3-pass *instrument → workload → use* loop (`compile.py:17412-17413`, host-side LLVM PGO via `instrument_flags`/`-fprofile-generate` at `compile.py:3491-3520` and `-fprofile-use` at `compile.py:3531-3554`); the PGO state (workload hash) is recorded so subsequent runs short-circuit when the workload matches.
260	
261	**The resumable Optuna-TPE search.** `--mode bayesian` (default) drives an Optuna TPE study (`TPESampler`, `compile.py:6549`) that **persists to a SQLite DB** at `<out_dir>/optuna_<opt>_<model>_<arch>.db` (`compile.py:16703-16704`) and is created with `load_if_exists=True` (`compile.py:6554-6556`) — so a Ctrl-C'd or cross-run sweep resumes its prior trials. `n_trials=None` means **no fixed budget**: a `BayesianEarlyStopper` (plateau Δ, EI floor, coverage-growth floor, wall-clock cap) governs convergence and `max_trials` is only a safety rail (`compile.py:16608-16624`). `--mode exhaustive` instead streams *every* prefilter survivor uncapped (`compile.py:16330-16346`). After TPE, a refine stage perturbs the top-K with ±2-step neighbours (elbow-detected when `top_k=None`, `compile.py:16917-16930`).
262	
263	**The learned cost-model pruning** (`CostModel`, `compile.py:5551`) is **default-ON** and genuinely prunes: an XGBoost regressor (with sklearn → numpy-ridge fallback chain, `compile.py:5595-5647`) is retrained every `cost_model_retrain_every` completed trials (`compile.py:16632-16635`, retrain hook wraps the timer at `compile.py:16838`) and rejects predicted-slow TPE suggestions *before building* them — each skip saves a ~5-min compile. Two independent gates with their own rejection caps: an absolute-threshold gate vs `best_so_far`, and a multi-fidelity cheap-proxy gate against the rolling-window timing quantile (`compile.py:16410-16427,16898-16915`). It can warm-start from a persisted sibling-optimizer model (transfer learning, `compile.py:16653-16676`).
264	
265	**`pick_winner`** (`compile.py:6824`) is the selection authority — covered next.
266	
267	### The fp64-gate-in-loop correctness hook
268	
269	This is the marquee correctness fix (task #28). The sweep's *timing* objective uses a cheap **same-dtype strict-fp32 self-consistency** oracle (variant-vs-strict-build of the same source). That oracle is unsafe to *select* on: two kernels sharing a rounding error agree, and an IL=4 reduction-order config can clear `np.allclose` yet be non-deterministic. So the winner is additionally gated against the **fp64 ground truth + A/A/A bit-determinism**:
270	
271	- `_default_correctness_hook(spec)` (`compile.py:7215`) builds a callable `hook(candidate_trial) -> bool` that calls `run_cell_gate(cell_key)` from `tests/hw/test_l3tc_tail_gate.py` (`compile.py:7261-7277`). It returns `None` (→ historical timing-only selection) unless a GPU + built extension are present *and* the `(optimizer, model)` maps to a registered gate cell (`correctness_cell_key`, `compile.py:7253-7268`).
272	- `_jit_autotune` **installs** the hook on `spec.correctness_hook` on the GPU path just before dispatching the driver, unless the caller supplied one (`compile.py:16303-16319`).
273	- `pick_winner` then **re-checks the top-`correctness_top_k` (default 3) candidate winners** by ascending timing; the first candidate the hook accepts wins, a failure is **demoted** to the next-best, and a hook that *raises* is treated as a failure (fail-closed) (`compile.py:6928-6974`). If no top-K candidate clears it, the winner is left **UNSET** rather than shipping an unchecked one (`compile.py:6968-6974`). It is wired through at the call site with `strict_numerics`/`allow_nondeterministic`/`correctness_hook` (`compile.py:16957-16962`).
274	
275	The hook ultimately reaches `_build_cell(model)` (`tests/hw/test_l3tc_tail_gate.py:551`), which builds the live race model from `g.DEFAULT_CONFIG` (`:561-569`).
276	
277	> **RG4-scale caveat (a real, load-bearing discrepancy).** The compile.py hook comments repeatedly claim the re-check runs "at PRODUCTION scale (d=2048)" (`compile.py:7222`, `:6857`, `:8745`). It does **not**. `_build_cell` uses `grokking_race_v2.DEFAULT_CONFIG`, whose model is `dim_model: 128, num_layers: 2` (`grokking_race_v2.py:261`) — the small modular-arithmetic grokking-race ("RG4") scale, *not* the 1B-scale preset (decoder `dim_model 1600`, mamba `2048`, `grokking_race_v2.py:251-253`). So the in-loop fp64 oracle certifies correctness at d=128, and a winner whose tile/split-K geometry only manifests at production scale is **NOT** re-gated at d=2048 by this hook. The authoritative d=2048 check still lives only in the out-of-band hardware gate. **A senior engineer resuming this work should re-gate any non-default shape winner at d=2048 before shipping**, and treat the "production-scale" comments as aspirational. (The roofline %-of-peak secondary *does* use `_PRODUCTION_ROOFLINE_D = 2048`, `compile.py:7002` — but that is a reported number, not the parity gate's model size.)
278	
279	`pick_winner` enforces several other filters unconditionally: drop `numerical_fail`; drop `non_deterministic` unless `--allow-nondeterministic` (the IL=4 trap, closed by default, `compile.py:6873-6883`); a generated/transformed `origin` in `_VALIDATION_REQUIRED_ORIGINS` is ineligible unless it recorded a strict-oracle PASS (`compile.py:6884-6892`); and **tiered-spill re-rank** — trials whose parsed ptxas-v report shows nonzero local-memory spill (`_trial_spill_breach`, `compile.py:7029`) are demoted *below* all clean trials in the sort key (re-rank, not hard-exclude, so correctness can still reach a spilling-but-correct trial, `compile.py:6898-6927`). Spill reaction (#23) and the roofline %-of-peak / sub-ceiling flag (#24, `_SUB_CEILING_PCT=0.10`, `compile.py:6977-7002`) are now *implemented* — the COMPILE_AUDIT listed them as gaps, but the current tree has the code.

302	The **dead-dim discipline** is central (`compile.py:1248-1303`). 306	### The macro-injection floor (`_tuned_inject`) and byte-identical no-JSON builds
307	
308	`compile.py`'s autotuner produces winners; **`grokking_optimizers/_tuned_inject.py`** is the *single source of truth* for making those winners ACTIVE in the shipped `_ops*.so` (lever (b)). It is **pure-stdlib** by design (`_tuned_inject.py:25-31`) so `setup.py` and a CPU-only unit test can import it by file path without triggering `grokking_optimizers/__init__.py` (which imports torch + probes CUDA).
309	
310	- **Producer:** `build_jit` calls `_export_kernel_tuned_json` → `export_winner` the moment a JIT winner is decided (`compile.py:17763`, `_tuned_inject.py:610`), atomically read-merge-writing the canonical `grokking_optimizers/_kernel_tuned.json` (`_tuned_inject.py:725,731`). Schema is **nested per-model** `{arch: {model: {optimizer: combo}}}` (`#12`, `_tuned_inject.py:17-23`) so tuning the same optimizer on a second model no longer last-wins; an old flat `{arch:{optimizer}}` block is migrated in place on the next write and still *read* for back-compat (`_tuned_inject.py:330-363,669-689`).
311	- **Consumer:** `setup.py`'s `TunedBuildExtension` reads the JSON and, per CUDA TU, appends `-DSG_TUNED_*` macros (+ `--maxrregcount=N` when nonzero) by monkeypatching torch's ninja writer and rewriting each build edge's `cuda_post_cflags` (`_tuned_inject.py:758-818`). TU→optimizer mapping is filename-based: `launch_<opt>.cu` and `mega_<model>_<opt>.cu` get their optimizer's flags; everything else (bindings, model-only TUs) gets none (`optimizer_for_source`, `_tuned_inject.py:228-257`; `model_for_source` selects the per-model winner, `:260-295`).

313	The **SAFE floor** is the `MACROS` table (`_tuned_inject.py:151-161`): `mega_block`, `tile_m`, `tile_n`, `dec_dw_splitk`, `vit_dw_splitk`, `prod_regs`, `cons_regs` (each `-D<macro>=<v>`) plus `maxrregcount` (real ptxas flag, `0`=unset=emit nothing). Each entry records its **in-source `#ifndef` default** (e.g. `SG_TUNED_PROD_REGS=40`, `SG_TUNED_CONS_REGS=232`, `dec_dw_splitk=1`, `vit_dw_splitk=4`) so:

315	1. a **no-JSON build is byte-identical** to the committed kernel (no `-D` emitted at all when there is no winner; `load_tuned` returns `None` → `[]`, `_tuned_inject.py:520-535`), and

322	### The Level-2 superoptimizer (#27, owner chose option (b))
323	
324	`SUPEROPTIMIZER_SCOPING.md` (#25) measured a **no-go** for a full generative superoptimizer; the owner overrode the *recommendation* (not the *constraints*) and chose **(b): make Level-2 REAL, correctness-gated** (`SUPEROPTIMIZER_L2_PLAN.md:1-8`). Level-2 = Level-1's flag/macro search *plus* a generative structural-rewrite layer that emits new *sources* (synth, polyhedral, native-wgmma, CUTLASS/CK) rather than just new `-DSG_TUNED_*` values (`SUPEROPTIMIZER_L2_PLAN.md:46-48`).
325	
326	**Current state: the scaffold is structurally wired but non-functional on the real path.** All five generative origins have honest origin-tagging (`ORIGIN_SYNTH`/`POLYHEDRAL`/`CUTLASS`/`CK`/`FASTMATH`, `compile.py:6791-6796`), the `_VALIDATION_REQUIRED_ORIGINS` winner gate (`compile.py:6806-6808`), and the source-swap are real and **fail-closed** — but:
327	
328	- **The C0 fragment-emitter blocker is the real obstacle.** The emitter seam routes through `grokking_optimizers.codegen.emit_variant_source` when `spec.enable_emitter` is on (`compile.py:14630-14647`) — but **that module does not exist** (verified: no `grokking_optimizers/codegen.py`). The import hits the `except`, emits a loud warn-once (MED.6, `compile.py:14648-14661`), and falls back to a macros-only build; `_emitted_sources` is never populated. Worse, even the synth/polyhedral lowerers that *do* emit compilable CUDA emit a **standalone host-launch `__global__` kernel** with its own grid — `synth_elementwise_*` / `_emit_reduce_cuda` / `_emit_scan_cuda` all emit `__global__ void` (`compile.py:30039,30156,30490`) and polyhedral emits `launch_polyhedral_kernel` (`compile.py:29234`). This is **the C2 constraint** (`SUPEROPTIMIZER_SCOPING.md:120-133`): the persistent fused megakernel owns its grid and runs fwd+bwd+dW+optimizer between hand-built grid barriers; a host-launched collective cannot run device-side inside it. The fix (Phase C0, `SUPEROPTIMIZER_L2_PLAN.md:129-139`) is to **re-target the emitter to emit a device-inlinable `__device__` tile/epilogue fragment** spliced between barriers, NOT a launchable kernel — the genuine prerequisite the scoping no-go was pricing.
329	- **Native wgmma/tcgen05/mfma/wmma mainloop is a hard-OFF zero-fragment stub.** `_MMA_NATIVE_LOADS_WIRED = False` (`compile.py:30179`): the native bodies never stage real A/B tiles (cp.async dest is a literal `0` / explicitly-zeroed register fragments), so on the target arch they would compute on zeros. Until the loads are wired, `_gemm_native_mma_mainloop` returns `None` with a loud warn-once and the caller emits a numerically-correct **scalar triple-loop** fallback (`compile.py:30202-30232`). This deliberately avoids the silent-zero numerical bug. Per the re-spec, Phase C **sidesteps the GEMM synth entirely** (the hand engine is near-maximal) and synthesizes the *fusion* (the fp32 epilogue passes) on the real elementwise/reduce lowerers (`SUPEROPTIMIZER_L2_PLAN.md:118-127`).
330	- **Polyhedral** is opt-in (`enable_polyhedral=False`, `compile.py:8622,17964`) and gated on `spec.config["polyhedral"]["enable"]`; the hook reads the `_emitted_sources` the dead emitter never sets (so unreachable today), and `libclang`/`islpy` are soft deps — when absent, legality is heuristic and **every** polyhedral variant is forced behind the strict on-device oracle (`compile.py:15733-15766`). It only stamps `ORIGIN_POLYHEDRAL` when a transformed source actually lands on disk and is built (`compile.py:15794-15802`) — the prior fake-green (template wearing a polyhedral tag) was fixed.
331	
332	**Correctness-gating is what makes this safe.** Because `pick_winner` makes any generated origin ineligible without a strict-oracle PASS, today's toy outputs would be correctly *rejected* — no fake-green. The remaining fake-green (#2 in the audit) — `build_jit`'s final source-swap checking only `== ORIGIN_SYNTH` and shipping the template for a polyhedral winner — has been **fixed**: it now swaps for any `origin in _SOURCE_GENERATING_ORIGINS` (= `_VALIDATION_REQUIRED_ORIGINS − {fastmath}`, `compile.py:6820-6821`), recovering the stashed generated source from `spec._emitted_sources["<ckey>:<origin>"]` and warning-and-falling-back-to-template if it cannot (`compile.py:17828-17872`). The fp64 oracle-in-loop (A2) is **landed** for the flag/macro path; the per-generated-candidate rebuild-before-fp64-gate is Phase-C0-coupled (there are no generated candidates today, so A2 is correct as-is, `SUPEROPTIMIZER_L2_PLAN.md:188-199`). The binding constraints — **C1** transport-only legality (ascending-k fp32 reduction order is non-associative; any reassociation fails the determinism gate), **C2** no-IR-expresses-the-megakernel, **C3** fp64-in-loop, **C4** the pattern library must contain the lever — are documented at `SUPEROPTIMIZER_L2_PLAN.md:49-74` and `SUPEROPTIMIZER_SCOPING.md:111-133,222-235`.

334	### Portability, the `--self-test` harness, and the build env
335	
336	**The `tune_hook` seam** (`BuildSpec.tune_hook`, `compile.py:8611`) is the schema-agnostic portability seam: a project declares `[project] tune_hook = "pkg.module:fn"` in `compile_config.toml`, and the autotuner invokes that callable in a fresh subprocess per built `.so` with the contract `fn(*, so_path, model, optimizer, arch, regime, seed) -> {"output": np.ndarray, "elapsed_ms": float}` (`compile.py:8599-8623`, `_hook_capture` at `:14376-14417`). compile.py compares `output` (variant vs strict-math reference build) for correctness and uses `elapsed_ms` for timing — knowing nothing about the op. This is how the persistent megakernel (reached via a pybind `fused_step`, not a discoverable `torch.op`) plugs in. When no `tune_hook` is set but `capture_workload` is, a lighter portable reference-capture path is used (`compile.py:15175-15180,15455-15469`).
337	
338	**Multi-arch dispatch** is table-driven: `ArchEntry` (`compile.py:434`) is the single source of truth per arch (vendor cuda/hip/pallas, gencode flags, smem/reg/warp limits, features, `l2_bytes`, and the `peak_tf`/`peak_bw` roofline constants added for #24, `compile.py:475+`). Per-arch space builders (`_sm90_full_space`, `_build_cuda_space`/`_build_cdna_space`/`_build_rdna_space`/`_build_pallas_space`) dispatch on vendor; `get_arch_entry` (`compile.py:1163`) routes pallas → `PallasTimer` and cuda/hip → the variant-`.so` timer. (Caveat the audit raised: Blackwell `sm_100a/103a/120a` route through the generic `_build_cuda_space`, so the rich TC tile surface is really sm_90-only today.)

352	## Why it is latency-bound + the roofline reality + the perf methods
353	
354	This section is the project owner's primary concern: an honest accounting of *where the time actually goes* at the roofline scale, *why* the megakernel sits far below the bf16 tensor-core peak, and *which perf levers won or lost and why*. Every number below is from the fresh re-profile (`/workspace/SuperGrok1.5/.perf/batch/decoder_reprofile_coarse.txt`, `decoder_reprofile_fwdfine.txt`) and the verdict ledger (`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md`), cross-checked against the source.

The roofline % is **derived from measured wall-time**, not a formal hardware score — that formal objective is the still-pending `#24` (`PLANNING_INPUT.md:16`). Two honesty caveats apply to every number below and the owner has insisted they be stated plainly:

388	### WHY it is latency-bound — the three mechanisms
389	
390	This is the load-bearing claim and it is honest: the gap is **fixable inefficiency, not an Amdahl wall of unavoidable non-GEMM compute.**
391	
392	**(a) The GEMM phases are ~11× slower than the ideal tensor-core time, and the gap is fixable, not compute-Amdahl.** The matmuls' *ideal* TC time is 3.961e13 FLOPs / 989.4 TF/s = **40.0 ms** (verified). Yet the GEMM-engine phases (P1_fwd + P1_bwd + P2_dW) take **~462 ms**. That ~420 ms gap is NOT "the rest is non-GEMM work the roofline can't count" — these phases *are* the GEMM phases. The gap decomposes into four fixable inefficiencies:
393	- **~20% barrier serialization** — slowest-CTA-gated grid-syncs (above), pure idle, attackable by phase overlap / fewer barriers / async.
394	- **The hand-rolled persistent wgmma running well below cuBLAS-class efficiency.** The engine lives in the persistent megakernel, so it cannot call a host-launched collective: `csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/mma.cuh` is a real Sm90 TMA+wgmma collective but is "explicitly REJECTED for the persistent-megakernel path" (`PERF_ANALYSIS.md:49-50`) — a host collective can't run device-side inside the persistent grid. So the fix is bringing CUTLASS-class *technique* (multi-stage pipeline, TMA, swizzle, warp-specialization) into the hand-rolled engine, whose primitives already exist.
395	- **Non-GEMM work serialized rather than overlapped under the matmuls** — the ~10 `__syncthreads`-separated fp32 epilogue passes per layer (bias, GELU, residual, LN) run *between* GEMMs instead of hiding under them (`PERF_ANALYSIS.md:38`, the P1-epilogue-fusion lever).
396	- **1 CTA/SM giving low occupancy to hide HBM latency.** The persistent grid-barrier *requires* ≥1 CTA/SM — the launcher REFUSES to launch (`cudaErrorLaunchOutOfResources`) if occupancy < 1 (`model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:180-181`; mirrored in `fused_mamba_megakernel.cuh:330`, `model_stage_vit.cuh:68`). At exactly one resident CTA/SM there is little latency-hiding slack; this is the structural cost of the no-cooperative-launch / hand-built GridBarrier design.
397	
398	**(b) It is NOT bandwidth-bound either.** Arithmetic intensities are **3,252–12,239 FLOP/byte** (table above), far past the ~295 FLOP/byte ridge — and HBM traffic is only 0.003–0.16% of 3.35 TB/s (`.perf/phase1_status_audit.md:18`). Both the compute roof (6.48%) and the bandwidth roof are far away, so the step sits in a **third LATENCY regime below both roofs**: it is gated by serialization, drain/wait stalls, and single-CTA occupancy, not by either roofline edge.
399	
400	**(c) The fwd/dX rings are now WGMMA-COMPUTE-bound, not drain-bound — the deeper-ring KEEP already hid the cp.async drain.** This is the freshest and most important refute. The `--fwd-fine` sub-profiler (`decoder_reprofile_fwdfine.txt:23-37`) splits the GEMM ring into ISSUE(cp.async) / WAIT(drain) / WGMMA(mma) / EPI / BARRIER:
401	- P1_fwd ring: WGMMA **46.6%** vs WAIT(drain) only **9.9%** → "COMPUTE/EPI-bound → deeper ring unlikely to help" (`:30`).
402	- P1_bwd(dX) ring: WGMMA **40.2%** vs WAIT **5.8%** → same verdict (`:37`).
403	
404	Before the deeper-ring KEEP the same profiler showed fwd WAIT 43% vs WGMMA 31% and dX WAIT 56% vs 20% — i.e. it *was* drain-bound, deeper prefetch *was* the right lever, and it worked (`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:64-67`). Now the drain is hidden, so **S>4 buffering is measured-unlikely to help on the decoder** (`PLANNING_INPUT.md:13-14`, `.perf/phase1_status_audit.md:19`). The remaining fwd/dX headroom is in GEMM *efficiency* (tiling / TILE_M / interleave / occupancy / register pressure), not more buffering (`PLANNING_INPUT.md:26-28`).

406	### The design goal (owner directive): high % of roofline at EVERY scale
407	
408	The directive is a high roofline fraction at *every* scale, and the diagnosis says that is largely achievable at the large shapes. At d=2048 the decoder's 6.48% is **mostly fixable inefficiency** (barrier serialization, sub-cuBLAS engine, un-overlapped epilogues, one-CTA occupancy) — the realistic target is 30–50%+, established by the proof point that the "~2% roofline was a STAGING artifact, not a hardware ceiling" (`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:61`, the dW-staging win that *doubled* the fraction). Crucially, **the fusion-vs-occupancy trade-off flips sign with scale**: the megakernel's aggressive fusion (one persistent kernel, 1 CTA/SM) pays off at large shapes where the GEMMs dominate and grid-barrier serialization is amortizable, but the same one-CTA/SM constraint that enforces the grid barrier *starves* latency-hiding at the smallest shapes where there isn't enough GEMM work to fill an SM.

428	## The correctness methodology (the HARD gate, transport-only rewrites, the ratchet)
429	
430	This system is an aggressive performance project — a hand-built persistent megakernel, an autotuner that rewrites kernels, and a long series of structural perf levers — bolted onto a correctness contract that *never* moves. The discipline that makes that safe is a single non-negotiable **HARD gate** plus a **keep/revert ratchet** layered on top of it, and a hard-won catalogue of *fake-green* hazards that the gate machinery is specifically shaped to catch. Everything below is the "how do we know a change is correct, and how do we decide whether to keep it" half of the project.
431	
432	### The HARD gate: fp64 parity + A/A/A bit-determinism
433	
434	Every change must clear two checks, ANDed together, before it can be considered at all. The canonical statement of the verdict rule is in the ledger header: *"apply → build → fp64 parity HARD-gate + A/A/A determinism → 3-seed timing at the roofline scale → KEEP iff faster on 3+ seeds AND parity-clean, else REVERT. Parity/determinism is a gate, not a tiebreaker"* (`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:5-8`).
435	
436	**(1) fp64 parity.** The bf16 wgmma megakernel is compared against a *pure-fp64* ground-truth oracle, run at the same shape, with the kernel's bf16 stays the compute precision and fp64 used only as the yardstick (`tests/hw/test_l3tc_tail_gate.py:11-13`). The per-cell harness `run_cell_gate` (`test_l3tc_tail_gate.py:1062`) runs one production L3-TC step through the exact route the race takes (`fused_train_step(..., gemm_impl="wgmma")`, `:1103-1105`), captures the TC-reduced grad and post-step params, and compares against the **canonical fp64 transcription** of the same single source the kernel compiles from (`csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h` → `ref_<opt>_step` in `test_reference_parity.py`, imported at `:1133-1135`). The comparison is structured in two surfaces:
437	- **(1a) params**, max-relative, default tolerance **1e-4** (`param_tol`, `:1346-1347`). 1e-4 is the *fp32-reorder band*: the kernel's elementwise tail rounds in fp32 in a different association order than the fp64 reference, and 1e-4 is the documented envelope for that (`:1336-1337`). Cells whose update goes through a non-tail numeric path widen it deliberately and document why: Muon's 2D weights run a 5-iteration Newton–Schulz that accumulates ~2e-3 fp32-vs-fp64, so muon uses `param_tol=2e-3` (`:399,408,1342-1345`).
438	- **(1b) state**, the *decisive* check, tolerance **1e-4** on `[m|v|extra]` (`:1369`). The docstring at `:1352-1359` explains why state, not params, is load-bearing: at step 1 every Adam-family tail collapses to ≈sign(g_amp) in the param update, so (1a) is blind to per-layer β1, amplification magnitude, and *state initialization* — all of which live in the state, not the sign. The grokfast `ema=g0` cold-start is the worked example: a kernel that inited `ema=0` matches params but diverges ~50× in the ema slice (`:1356-1359`).
439	
440	The SAM-tier surfaces carry a *floor* tolerance instead of the reorder band, because a second backward through a bf16 kernel cannot reach fp32 reorder: **SAM sharpness/sam_dir use 3e-2 / 2.5e-2** (`test_l3tc_tail_gate.py:27-28`, `:439,445,476`). These are explicitly the bf16-TC-vs-pure-fp64 *measured floor* (~2.2e-2 sharpness / 1.87e-2 sam_dir), with the tol set above it (`:634,730`). The looksam sam_dir check is fed the kernel's *own* cached direction and validated against a pure-fp64 second backward perturbed by `ron·g` (`:1161-1224`), with a liveness assert that the oracle direction is `>1e-6` so the parity can never be vacuously satisfied by a skipped SAM phase (`:1222-1224`).
441	
442	**(2) A/A/A bit-determinism.** The production step is re-run 3× from the same init with fresh state, and loss/grad/params must be **bit-identical** under `torch.equal` (`:1396-1411`). This is `torch.equal` exactly — not a tolerance — across `(L1==L2==L3)`, `equal(G1,G2)`, `equal(P1,P2)` (`:1410-1411`); the SAM cells extend it to `mu` and `sharpness` slices (`:866-869`). Determinism is achieved by *construction*, not luck: fixed batch→CTA ownership and ascending-CTA / ascending-k fp32 reduction order (`tests/hw/test_l3tc_tail_gate.py:6-7`; the mechanism is spelled out in `csrc/fused/sm_90/dec_weights.cuh:59-79` — fixed contiguous batch slices, single-writer per-element owner, one grid barrier, then a cross-CTA reduce summing partials *in ascending CTA index*).
443	
444	The two checks are ANDed (`ok = tail_ok and det_ok`, `:1417`), and that conjunction is the HARD gate. The autotuner is wired to the *same* gate: `_default_correctness_hook` (`compile.py:7215`) builds a `pick_winner` hook that re-runs `run_cell_gate` and demotes any candidate that fails either leg, fail-closed (a raising hook is treated as a demotion, `:7250-7251,7277`). This was added precisely because the tuner's own timing oracle is fp32 self-consistency, which two co-wrong kernels can both pass — see the IL=4 hazard below.
445	
446	### Transport-only legal rewrites vs NEEDS-PARITY changes
447	
448	The rewrite rule that lets the project move fast: **a rewrite may reorder data movement freely, but it must PRESERVE the ascending-k fp32 reduction order.** If it does, bit-determinism and parity hold automatically and the change is *transport-only* — no re-gating drama. If it changes the numeric association, it is **NEEDS-PARITY**: it produces a valid-but-different fp32 reassociation that the gate must arbitrate against the 1e-4 reorder band.
449	
450	Concrete examples the codebase ships:
451	
452	- **ViT B1 sub-tiling (`SG_TUNED_VIT_P1_SUBTILE_S`)** is the canonical worked case. Decoupling P1 *scheduling* granularity from the 1088-row GEMM tile changes which global rows land in which CTA. The kernel comment classifies the surfaces precisely (`model_stage_vit_tc.cuh:150-162`): dW / biases / cls / pos grads are **byte-identical** (P2 reads activations by global token row and contracts ascending-k independent of P1 tiling, and each row is a sample-local function preserved by the whole-sample invariant), but the 10 LN-affine γ/β grads and the loss are **valid fp32 REASSOCIATIONS** — regrouping which rows sum into which CTA shifts the low bits — *"absorbed by the gate's 1e-4 fp32-reorder tol (the decoder already ships TILE_M 64/256 through the same gate)."* A/A/A still holds because S is fixed across the 3 runs (a fixed deterministic partition). The explicit conclusion: *"OFF = byte-identical; ON = a NEEDS-PARITY swept dim, the GPU fp64 + A/A/A gate is the arbiter"* (`:161-162`). The whole-sample invariant is a hard `static_assert` (`:239`).
453	
454	- **decoder `SG_TUNED_TILE_M` 64/256** is the named precedent the ViT comment leans on: changing the token-tile row count is a valid fp32 reassociation of the same reduction, lands inside 1e-4, and the decoder already ships those alternates through the same gate (`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:40` records TILE_M→256 as SKIP +27.7% *on perf*, i.e. it was parity-legal and only lost on speed).
455	
456	- **split-K dW (`SG_TUNED_*_DW_SPLITK`, factor G)** is the transport-only case that *does* preserve order. Splitting a tile's K-contraction across G CTAs adds parallelism, but the partials are summed by *"a deterministic ascending-chunk reduce ... no float atomics, fixed order → parity + A/A/A bit-determinism hold"*, and `G==1` routes to the byte-identical single-CTA path (`model_stage_vit_tc.cuh:97-104`; `fused_vit_megakernel.cuh:394`). Because the summation order is preserved, split-K is a transport-only rewrite — which is why it could be *kept* (decoder DW split-K 4→2, `OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:36`).
457	
458	The same "order lives in the summation, not who computes it" principle governs the cross-CTA optimizer reductions (Prodigy's global-d, GrokAdamW's grad-norm clip, Muon's Frobenius norm): they were deliberately moved off the *work-stealing task queue* (whose claim order varies run-to-run → non-associative fp32 regrouping → A/A/A violation) onto a **fixed contiguous element range per CTA + ascending-CTA owner-sum** (`fused_vit_megakernel.cuh:874-888`). The IL=4 reject (below) is the cautionary case where this discipline was violated.
459	
460	### The keep/revert ratchet (the P-series discipline)
461	
462	Once a change is parity-clean, perf decides its fate, and the rule is asymmetric on purpose: **parity is a hard gate; perf must be better on 3+ seeds to KEEP, else REVERT** (`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:5-8`). "Neutral" (no measurable gain) counts as not-positive and reverts. On any revert, the *mechanism* is root-caused and used to redirect the next decision (`:8`). The ledger is the canonical record of every KEEP / REVERT / NEUTRAL / SKIP with its why; representative entries:
463	- **KEEP**: decoder cp.async-ring −14.2% across all decoder cells (`Track A` 0005, `:24`); decoder DW split-K 4→2 −2.5% (`:36`); the Track-E dW staging fix 2.05× (`:61`).
464	- **REVERT**: vit SAM-scoped outline +5% slower (`:22`); the P0 decoder dW pipelined GEMM — *fp64 gate PASSED (correct), but perf regressed −11.6%*, root-caused to the dW being staging-bound not drain-bound, which then *redirected* the campaign to staging (`Track E` P0, `:52`).
465	- **REJECT** with the sharpest lesson: decoder GEMM interleave 2→4 was the **fastest** lever found (bench −9.3%) but **A/A/A FAILED** on all 10 decoder cells (IL=4 makes the dW M-atom groups 4-wide and the ragged atom counts make the 4-wide group-reduce non-deterministic). It ran fine and faster at d=2048 where atoms divide evenly, *so the bench missed it; the gate caught it.* The recorded takeaway: *"bench-first is necessary, NOT sufficient — every winner must clear the full A/A/A gate"* (`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:37`).
466	
467	The structural safety net under the ratchet is **byte-identical OFF defaults for risky knobs**: a NEEDS-PARITY knob must `#if`-erase to the exact pre-knob kernel when off, so a never-engaged lever is provably inert. ViT subtile-S at the default value compiles the m_real row-guard and runtime-m_atoms code out entirely → *"the OFF build is BYTE-IDENTICAL"* (`model_stage_vit_tc.cuh:143-146`, guarded by `#if SG_TUNED_VIT_P1_SUBTILE_S < 64` at `:391`); split-K `G==1` takes the no-scratch single-CTA path (`model_stage_vit_tc.cuh:103-104`); the GEMM interleave width 1 is the bit-for-bit serial path (`:117`). This is what lets the autotuner expand the search space without risking the shipped default.
468	
469	### Fake-green / oracle-trust hazards (and how they are caught)
470	
471	The recurring failure mode this project keeps hitting is not a wrong kernel that *fails* a gate — it is a **fake-green**: a gate that passes while the thing it claims to verify is broken, usually because the oracle co-derives with the kernel or the discriminating instrument never runs. The standing audits (`.perf/oracle_trust_audit.json`, `.perf/test_coverage_gap_audit.json`) exist to hunt this class. The catalogue:
472	
473	- **The macro-drift guard (table-vs-header).** The autotuner emits `-DSG_TUNED_*` flags from a hand-maintained `MACROS` table; if that table drifts from the kernels' `#ifndef SG_TUNED_*` guards, the tuner emits a `-D` no kernel reads (a silent no-op) or misses one. `header_default_macros()` (`_tuned_inject.py:198-208`) declares the asserted defaults, and `setup.py:_verify_macro_names` (`:944-970`) programmatically scans *all* of `csrc/` for the `#ifndef` guards and warns on any table macro not guarded anywhere. The audit note at `_tuned_inject.py:949-953` records *why* this had to become a tree-walk: the old single-file check pointed at a header (`kernels/sm_90/adamw_sm90.cuh`) deleted in the L3-TC-only cut, so it silently early-returned and *could never fire* — itself a fake-green.
474	
475	- **The SG11 co-wrong oracle (cos operand).** The historical incident class: the kernel computing `cos(grad, MU)` instead of canonical `cos(grad, MOMENTUM)` as the gate's second cosine operand (`oracle_trust_audit.json` finding 2). The cold step-1 gate is *structurally blind* to it: at step 1 `m0=0 ⇒ cos=0 ⇒ gate=sigmoid(0)=0.5` regardless of the operand (`test_l3tc_tail_gate.py:798-803`), and at the default `rescale=0.1` the gate-dependent surfaces are damped below the 1e-4 param tol by Adam v-normalization. The catching instrument is `run_sg11_warmup_gate` (`:882`), which runs warm-up steps so `momentum≠0 ∧ mu≠0` genuinely diverge, pumps `rescale=2.0` so the term is above tolerance (`:919`), recovers the kernel's gate and asserts it matches `cos(grad,momentum)` AND *not* `cos(grad,mu)` — `gate_ok = (err_vs_momentum < 1e-2) and (err_vs_mu > 1e-1)`, two regimes separated by ~3 orders of magnitude (`:1009-1013`), with a non-vacuity assert that the warm-up actually exercised the divergence (`gate_div > 1e-4`, `:1054-1057`). The oracle-trust audit's *open* finding is that this discriminating test is **CLI-only (`--sg11-warmup`)** and never collected by pytest/CI (`oracle_trust_audit.json` finding 2; `test_coverage_gap_audit.json` RG1), so the CI path is still structurally pinned to gate=0.5 — a live coverage gap, not yet closed.
476	
477	- **The autotune-hook d=128-vs-d=2048 scale lie.** `_default_correctness_hook`'s docstring promises *"PRODUCTION-scale (d=2048)"* validation (`compile.py:7220-7222`) and the inner comment repeats *"the SAME cell gate at production scale"* (`:7271-7274`), but the body calls `_run_cell_gate(cell_key)` (`:7277`) → `_build_cell` at the toy grokking scale (p=97, baked d=128, `test_l3tc_tail_gate.py:551,564`). There is no d=2048 rebuild anywhere in the hook. The audit flags this as exactly the SG11 shape — the validator's *claimed* scale and *actual* scale disagree — so a winner that is fp64-correct at d=128 but breaks at d=2048 (occupancy spill, tile-count-dependent reduction) is accepted and published (`test_coverage_gap_audit.json` RG4).
478	
479	- **The SG2 mirrored-oracle (real-rank de-mirror + voting fidelity probe).** SG2's B1 anchor is `sg2_kernel_mirror.oracle_step`, which re-implements the *kernel's low-rank* CSA lightning-indexer (drops `idx_UQ`, normalizes `/sqrt(rank)`) rather than the *canonical full-rank* path (`(x@idx_DQ)@idx_UQ`, `/sqrt(d)`) — so `kernel == oracle` by construction for the indexer top-k and B1 cannot distinguish a correct low-rank indexer from a buggy one (`oracle_trust_audit.json` finding 1). The required fix is to **de-mirror** the reference back to the canonical full-rank indexer, and to make the only divergence-detecting instrument — the **N>64 CSA fidelity probe** — *vote* in the verdict. Today that probe only `print`s under `if verbose` and sets no `_ok` flag (`_sg2_l3tc_gate.py:320-333`), and the gate verdict is `ok = b1_ok and aaa_ok and tie_ok` (`:335`) — so an indexer regression consistent with the low-rank mirror passes silently. The same toothlessness afflicts the SG2 tie-probe, which validates the *oracle's own* strategy-A perm builder (a property of the test helper) rather than the kernel's segmented sort (`:290-318`; `test_coverage_gap_audit.json` RG16).
480	
481	- **The `_emitted_sources` keying bug (polyhedral fake-green).** `build_jit`'s final source-swap checked *only* `origin == ORIGIN_SYNTH`, so a polyhedral/CUTLASS/CK winner left `final_sources = sources` (the un-optimized **template**) yet reported `origin=polyhedral` at the *winning* timing — a fake-green where the published artifact is not the thing that was timed. The fix generalizes the swap to any `origin in _VALIDATION_REQUIRED_ORIGINS` with a stashed `spec._emitted_sources[ckey:origin]` (`COMPILE_AUDIT.md:35-41`; the keyed stash is at `compile.py:6812,14645,8538`). The companion `_VALIDATION_REQUIRED_ORIGINS × {ok,deterministic}` winner gate is otherwise real and fail-closed (`COMPILE_AUDIT.md:15,165`).
482	
483	- **The IL=4 / atomicAdd determinism trap** (the origin of the autotune fp64-hook): the fp32 self-consistency oracle the sweep uses for timing cannot catch a non-deterministic reduction order, so a `non_deterministic` config that merely clears `np.allclose` could win unless `strict_numerics` was on. The fix rejects `numerical_status=="non_deterministic"` unconditionally by default (`COMPILE_AUDIT.md:43-47`; `compile.py:6873,19195,23667`), and the fp64 `_default_correctness_hook` was added so the tuner re-checks winners against the *out-of-band* hardware gate that originally caught it.
484	
485	The systematic prevention rules distilled from these incidents (`oracle_trust_audit.json` notes; `test_coverage_gap_audit.json` notes) are the project's standing oracle-trust doctrine: (1) **anchor direction** — every oracle's expected value derives from the canonical *algorithm* source, never from a restatement of what the kernel does; (2) **no two same-file twins** — an fp64 "oracle" and fp32 "mirror" differing only in precision/reduction shape fall to a single co-edit; (3) **operand-discrimination** — for any cosine/dot/selection, include a closed-form case where the correct and plausible-wrong operands give *different* answers and assert both equality-to-right and inequality-to-wrong; (4) **liveness = CI-collected and non-vacuous** — a discriminating instrument behind a CLI flag is not a guard; (5) **no silent reports** — any probe that surfaces a known divergence must set an `_ok` flag that votes in the boolean verdict.
486	
487	### The recurring full-codebase audit discipline
488	
489	The hazard catalogue is kept current by a *process*, not a one-off. The owner directive (`CODEBASE_AUDIT.md:3-6`) is: **after every landed step, run a comprehensive line-by-line analysis of the entire codebase** — modeled on the compile.py audit but tree-wide — hunting (1) bugs, (2) dead code to clean, (3) dead files to clean. "A step" is a landed commit (a KEEP/REVERT, a fix batch, a perf lever), and the audit runs *after* it is committed and gate-green, because auditing a mid-flight tree is wasteful (`:8-11`). Each run is an Opus swarm: contiguous range agents over `csrc/`, `grokking_optimizers/`, `tuning/`, `scripts/`, `tests/`, top-level, plus three cross-cutting agents — a **dead-file reachability graph** (import/include/build/test reachability), a **dead-code** symbol-never-called pass, and a **consistency** pass for duplicated/diverged logic (`:13-24`). Findings accumulate, deduped against prior runs, in `CODEBASE_AUDIT_FINDINGS.md` (`:25`). Deletion is conservative — *prove* a path is dead before removing, **flag-and-keep** anything ambiguous or not self-authored, and re-validate after every deletion, reverting anything that goes red (`:29-34`). Per-step runs re-sweep with deduped output but always re-run the cheap reachability graph to catch files newly orphaned by the step (`:37-39`). This is the loop that produced the two audit JSONs above and continues to surface the open coverage gaps (the SG11 warm-up gate not collected by CI, the autotune-hook scale lie, the non-voting SG2 probes) that future work must close.
